source_routes.name: About this data – fixed coverage and full-fibre take-up v2

guard_streams.write_limit: No second task, owner takeover or parallel runner is permitted.

facts.detail: The Spring update reports fixed broadband availability and mobile coverage as a January 2026 snapshot.
The interim update compares against Connected Nations 2025, whose underlying snapshot was July 2025.

guard_streams.write_limit: Publication dates and comparison periods cannot substitute for row-level source identity.

facts.detail: Full fibre is reported for 24.9 million residential premises, 82 percent of 30.5 million homes.
Gigabit-capable availability is reported for 27.1 million homes, or 89 percent.

guard_streams.write_limit: Residential national headlines cannot be assigned to all-premises postcode rows or parcels.

guard_streams.source: Ofcom Spring 2026 update and v2 data note

facts.detail: Ofcom states that headline gigabit-capable and full-fibre coverage focuses on residential properties.
Coverage for residential and commercial premises combined is supplied in the interactive report and downloadable files.

guard_streams.write_limit: Residential and all-premises denominators must remain separate.

guard_streams.source: Ofcom Spring 2026 update and v2 data note

facts.detail: Full-fibre take-up reached 12.4 million active broadband connections.
The reported 47 percent ratio uses all premises with full-fibre access and includes residential and commercial active lines.

guard_streams.write_limit: Active-line take-up is adoption, not availability or measured parcel throughput.

facts.detail: Ofcom estimates 4,000 premises without access to affordable decent broadband.
Ofcom separately reports 39,000 premises unable to access decent broadband from fixed line or FWA.

guard_streams.write_limit: Affordability and fixed/FWA technical-availability populations are not interchangeable.

facts.detail: Ofcom identifies approximately 7,000 additional commercial premises that could be eligible for the USO under the stated affordability condition.
Those commercial premises are excluded from the affordable-gap estimate because some may already have connectivity such as leased lines.

guard_streams.write_limit: Potential USO eligibility cannot be promoted as confirmed lack of connectivity.

facts.detail: Ofcom publishes separate fixed-broadband and mobile data downloads.
The FAQ states that speed information in these downloads is available only for fixed broadband.

guard_streams.write_limit: Mobile coverage evidence cannot fill fixed postcode speed fields.

facts.detail: The fixed-broadband coverage product describes maximum available speeds and accompanies each Connected Nations publication.
The fixed-broadband performance product concerns active customer connections and is published annually with the main report.

guard_streams.write_limit: Maximum available speed and active-connection performance are distinct measurement products.

facts.detail: Ofcom confirms that no Fixed Performance Postcode file has been published since the July 2024 methodology revision.
Ofcom considers overall average download-speed analysis robust down to local-authority level, not postcode level.

guard_streams.write_limit: No active-connection or average performance value may be inferred for a postcode or parcel.

guard_streams.source: Ofcom v2 data note and field-matrix screenshot

facts.detail: All Matched Premises counts locations matched to at least one fixed-provider record with a non-zero predicted download speed.
Premises not meeting that match condition are classified as unclassified.

guard_streams.write_limit: Unclassified does not prove zero coverage and cannot be converted to a parcel speed.

guard_streams.source: Ofcom v2 data note and field-matrix screenshot

facts.detail: The All Premises count field is present at all detailed levels except postcode.
The All Matched Premises count field is also absent from postcode files.

guard_streams.write_limit: Postcode percentages cannot be converted to exact counts without an official denominator.

facts.detail: Coverage fields refer to fixed-line broadband unless FWA is explicitly named in the field description.
The fixed-or-FWA decent-broadband field includes WISP or Mobile FWA and includes non-matched records and zero predicted speeds.

guard_streams.write_limit: Fixed-line, WISP and Mobile FWA semantics must remain field-specific.
